findings.F1: In folds B and C the tested cases replicate strongly. There are 86 cases on 52 days, with an unusual 3-day move of +4.33 % (t 4.87, cases of one day summed), a median of +2.9 % and 82 % of cases positive. Against step 5's 290 cases at +0.73 % (t 1.14), the roughly 204 cases in folds A and D must average about −0.8 %. So the result is unclear because the effect is strong in some folds and reversed in others, not because it is weak everywhere.
findings.F2: Inside folds B and C nothing in a coin's bars marks where the effect is absent. It is positive in every year: 2018 +4.5 % (t 1.47), 2019 +2.9 % (t 1.58), 2020 +3.6 % (t 3.07) and 2021 +5.2 % (t 3.59). It is positive on every coin, from ZEC +1.3 % to ADA +10.3 %, on the six core coins (+3.8 %, t 5.10) and on the others (+6.7 %, t 2.60). It is positive in every tercile of the 60-day return (+3.6 % to +6.2 %), the 5-day return (+3.0 % to +6.1 %) and the 30-day swing (+3.2 % to +4.2 %).
findings.F3: The move comes from the idea's situation, not from the rising calm market alone. Case cells beat the other rising-calm cells by +3.4 % (Welch t 4.41); those other cells move +0.92 % (t 1.47), and cells outside the profile move −0.19 %. Rising-calm days that close in the bottom quarter but are not wide move only +0.96 % (t 0.77, 59 cases), so the wide range is what matters.
findings.F4: The idea's grading by nearness to the low shows in B and C, but width grades the wrong way. By close location, the top tercile moves +6.5 % (t 3.25) against +2.8 % (t 2.41) for the bottom, with a Spearman of 0.22. By width, the narrowest tercile of the wide days moves +6.0 % against +2.6 % for the widest, with a Spearman of −0.17. So "wider means more" is not in the bars, while the idea's own gradient is.
findings.F5: The horizon is not where the test lost the effect. In B and C the next-day unusual move is +2.6 % (t 3.56), two days +2.9 % (t 3.14), three days +4.4 % (t 4.74) and five days +4.2 % (t 3.12). The plan's 3 days is the clearest reading.
findings.F6: The test already used every coin, fold and daily bar available (19 coins, folds A to D), so no more data can lift its t of 1.14. Its size is 0.101 of a usual 3-day move (8.85 %), and its total move of +1.17 % is 5.3 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade. If the effect held in every fold it would pay, but it does not hold in every fold.

no_ideas: The rebound is strong and present on every coin, year and sub-regime visible in folds B and C (F1, F2), yet it nets to about zero over all four folds. No condition read from a coin's bars at the close separates where it holds from where it reverses (F2, F4, F5), and the test already used all the data available (F6), so neither a narrower idea nor more data would give a clearer answer.
